title: A commutative-up-to-homotopy square induces a morphism of the cones
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-functorial-cone at source lines 643-662: for a differential graded algebra A and a square of homomorphisms of dg A-modules which is commutative up to homotopy, there is a morphism c : C(f_1) -> C(f_2) that together with the given vertical maps gives a morphism of the triangles (K_1, L_1, C(f_1), f_1, i_1, p_1) and (K_2, L_2, C(f_2), f_2, i_2, p_2) in the homotopy category. The proof at source lines 664-680 is short but it is the construction that makes the cone functorial, and the construction is the substance: it takes the homotopy h between f_2 a and b f_1, defines c by the block matrix with entries b, h, 0 and a on L_1 direct sum K_1, must verify by a matrix computation that this c commutes with the differentials (which is exactly where the homotopy is used, since in the strictly commutative case the off-diagonal entry would have to vanish), and then checks the two compatibility identities with the cone's inclusion and projection. The statement records none of the matrix, and the role of the homotopy in the differential computation is the point of the argument. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
